statement: The piece reports the group needs roughly $308 billion of annual AI revenue to break even on the planned capex against an estimated $183 billion of current AI revenue, an annual gap of about $125 billion.
why: A persistent break-even gap of this size is the mechanism by which capex plans get trimmed, so it is the main downside risk sitting under the buildout headlines.

impact.mechanism: If AI revenue stays well below the level required to cover depreciation on deployed capex, buyers slow future accelerator orders.

evidence.excerpt: the group requires roughly '$308 billion' in annual AI revenue to break even on the capex. Current AI revenues are estimated at '$183 billion,' leaving a gap of roughly '$125 billion' annually

confidence.basis: Break-even arithmetic attributed to unnamed strategists inside a social/wire aggregation; no primary research note located.

entity: hyperscalers (Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Oracle, Meta); Goldman Sachs
